title: docs: clarify that --ulimit size limits are in bytes
body:
Fixes: #25236

`--ulimit` values are passed through unchanged: `units.ParseUlimit()` is a plain
`strconv.ParseInt` (no scaling, no suffixes), the result lands in
`specs.POSIXRlimit`, and the runtime applies it via `setrlimit(2)` — where size
limits are byte-valued. So `--ulimit memlock=4096` correctly sets 4096 bytes.

The confusion comes from the display side: the `ulimit` shell builtin rescales
several resources when printing (kbytes for `-d`, `-l`, `-m`, `-s`; 512-byte
blocks for `-c`, `-f`), so 4096 bytes prints as `4`. `msgqueue` is also
byte-valued and prints raw, which shows the same pipeline with a different
display divisor.

As discussed in the issue, changing the units would silently shift every
existing memlock/stack/core/fsize/rss configuration by 1024x and break parity
with the Docker CLI, `containers.conf` `default_ulimits`, Quadlet `Ulimit=`, and
the kube ulimit annotation. So this is docs-only — **no behavior change.**

- `options/ulimit.md` (run, create, update, `podman-container.unit.5`): states
  the units are those of `setrlimit(2)`, adds a per-type unit table, a worked
  `memlock=4194304` -> `ulimit -l` = 4096 example, and notes that unit suffixes
  are not accepted.
- `options/ulimit.image.md` (build, farm build): short note that size limits are
  bytes, with a cross-reference to `podman-run(1)`.

Verified with `make docs` and by rendering the generated man pages; also ran
`hack/man-page-checker` and `hack/markdown-preprocess.t`.

Follow-up (happy to do separately if wanted): the parse error for
`--ulimit memlock=4096kb` currently surfaces only `strconv.ParseInt: parsing
"4096kb": invalid syntax`, which says nothing about units. Mentioning bytes
there would catch the first-time guess at the moment it happens.
